title: Format core: .mulch store reader/writer with ml 0.10.7 round-trip suite
description: Read and write the .mulch/ store natively: mulch.config.yaml (version, domains, governance, classification_defaults, optional prime/search knobs) and expertise/<domain>.jsonl records plus the soft-archive store archive/. Preserve unknown record fields on every write (additive fields are the only sanctioned extension mechanism — ADR-0023). Acceptance: round-trip suite where our writer writes a corpus, the reference ml 0.10.7 CLI reads and mutates it, and our additive fields survive (the ADR-0023 acceptance gate); canonical JSONL write order pinned. Probe the reference first (ml init/add/record on a temp store) before freezing the model. Deliverable: crates/mulch format core + round-trip test battery against a provisioned ml 0.10.7 reference (see the seeds repo's sd-reference fixture pattern). Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro (points 1-3, 6).

title: CLI parity: mulch command surface mirrors ml 0.10.7
description:
Implement the reference CLI surface (init, add, record, edit, query, setup, prime, onboard, status, validate, prune, archive, restore, search, rank, outcome, doctor, ready, sync, delete, delete-domain, move, learn, compact, config, diff, upgrade, completions, audit) command-for-command where the reference is the product: flags, --json envelope shapes, exit codes, and written store state pinned by a differential battery against a provisioned ml 0.10.7 reference. Help honesty rule: --help lists only implemented commands (seeds-repo deviation precedent). Deliberate divergences get documented in README DEVIATIONS with their own expectations, never silently. May be split into molecular seeds per command group at plan time. Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro; seeds-repo CLI-parity precedent (seeds-facc).

[2026-10-03, local iterate loop] Split at plan time (sanctioned above) into six molecular slice seeds: mulch-da8b (CLI skeleton + init/status/validate/doctor), mulch-fdd0 (add/record/edit/outcome), mulch-dc67 (delete/delete-domain/move), mulch-16da (query/prime/search/rank/ready/learn), mulch-7c55 (prune/archive/restore/compact), mulch-176f (config/sync/setup/onboard/audit/diff/upgrade/completions). This umbrella closes when all six slices are closed.

title: Self-hosting cutover: mulch binary replaces ml for this repo
description: Once format core + CLI parity hold: replace the bootstrap-phase jayminwest ml CLI (@os-eco/mulch-cli 0.10.7) with this repo's own `mulch` binary for THIS repo's .mulch/ store — the parity proof. Covers: cargo install path (just install), .mise.toml bootstrap entry removal, run-environment image update (the shared seeds-toolchain image gains the mulch binary additively — cross-repo change through denkhaus/seeds), the reference renamed ml-ref for the differential battery (sd-ref precedent), and AGENTS.md/loop wording updates. Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro (points 1, 6); seeds-repo self-hosting cutover precedent (seeds-3791).

title: Canonical-domain layer: alias resolution for fragmented domains
description: Mulch phase scope from ADR-0023 point 6: fix domain fragmentation (develop/dev-loop/develop-loop/develop-workflow/devloop/loop/loop-assets class) via ALIAS RESOLUTION — a resolution step that maps alias domains onto canonical ones at read/prime/query time. Strictly additive: existing domain files are never merged, moved, or rewritten destructively; aliases live in mulch.config.yaml. Needs the format core landed first (dependency, not ordering accident). Basis: ADR-0023 in denkhaus/fabro (point 6).

title: Enable terminal notifications for Deadlock/SoftStop parkings on the develop line
description:
Run settings notifications.terminal is currently enabled:false; enable it filtered to Deadlock/SoftStop terminal events only. Evidence: run 01M40KWWZ4M4P396PGCVH08Q6G ended clean, but a parked Needs-operator/Blocked run would sit silent for up to the tracker_guard stale_threshold_hours of 6.0 — the only other failure channel is the 6-hour stale-claim sweep. Expected effect: a human learns within minutes when a future run parks. This is an engine-side run-settings change, not a repo asset the develop line can implement — user decision and user action requested. Not capability-affecting (no agent-reachable tool/credential/env delta; host-side notification config only).
Basis: run 01M40KWWZ4M4P396PGCVH08Q6G, workflow version absent, commit f99626c4792a46666c7cfcfb9f1d1f65efe155b1

title: Store ownership: one deep .mulch store module (lenient | strict | raw-line policies, compact rewrite)
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 1, Strong). Evidence: the lib `Store` has ZERO callers in the binary; six readers and five writers implement the same file conventions independently (commands/mod.rs raw-line IO, status/validate/doctor lenient reads, records.rs strict reader/writer, ConfigStore writing mulch.config.yaml itself). Problem: the format contract lives in prose + duplicated IO; every one of the ~20 remaining parity commands needs another read+write of the same store. Solution: name the access policies (lenient | strict | raw-line for reads; rewrite-compact | append-verbatim for writes) in the lib store module and move the CLI's file IO behind them, starting with one pilot command (status). Benefits: locality (the reference semantics live in one place), leverage (each new command inherits the policies), tests (policy-level unit tests replace per-command store fixtures). Note: README DEVIATIONS pins the lenient/strict reader split as CONTRACT — the deepening must name both policies, never merge them. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html (temp, ephemeral).

[2026-10-03, local iterate loop] Sprint 4 pick (of the five arch-gate candidates + three remaining parity slices): the user said 'weiter' without naming one, so priority order decides — this is a Strong candidate and the gate's top recommendation, and it makes the remaining ~20 parity commands cheaper; the alternative Strong candidate (mulch-9e70, command boundary) is deliberately SECOND so it can reuse the seam this sprint creates.
closeReason: Store ownership landed (commits vwm + rlu): lib StoreFiles owns discovery (StoreLocation), config mutations (register/remove/delete domain, canonical write) and the explicit read/write policies (read_records strict with the allow-unknown escape hatch, read_lines for the reporting commands, rewrite_domain compact+id-generation, append_domain_line verbatim); ConfigStore and the CLI IO helpers deleted; the locate->message+channel policy has one owner (open_store); status/validate/doctor read through the seam; edit/outcome/record read strictly before any write. Standards + spec reviews fixed pre-close (the spec review caught a regression: the allow-unknown flag had been dropped by the first cut). 65-test battery green; 5 parity gaps surfaced by the review filed as seeds (ccf6, 351d, b88b, ca49, 7896).

title: Command boundary: one owner for locate + failure text + output channel
description: Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 2, Strong). Evidence: `render_error` is byte-identical in three files (delete.rs, delete_domain.rs, move_cmd.rs); the "not found in config" message exists in six shapes; Failure fields are poked from ~21 sites; the same 14-line store-location opening appears in ten commands. Problem: every new command re-derives the boundary rules (which message shape, which stream, which exit code). Solution: a mulch::Error -> reference-text adapter plus one boundary helper that takes the per-command text shape and the envelope channel as data. Benefits: locality (boundary rules in one module), leverage (new commands declare, not implement), tests (one table-driven test covers the matrix; per-command tests shrink to the command's own text). Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

title: Record-type registry: one table for the six types (payload fields, required fields, canonical order)
description: Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 3, Worth exploring). Evidence: PAYLOAD_TYPES lives in ids.rs, CANONICAL_ORDER + REQUIRED_FIELDS in record.rs, BRANCHES in commands/schema.rs — one registry with three owners across two crates. Solution: write the one-row-per-type registry table and diff it against all three existing lists FIRST (expose every disagreement), then collapse. Benefits: locality + leverage for the remaining record-touching commands. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

title: Canonical field order: one writer owns the record line layout
description: Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 4, Worth exploring). Evidence: build_record (flag path) ranks evidence BEFORE payload fields (probe-confirmed), while record.rs CANONICAL_ORDER ranks it after — two owners of the same order disagree, and only the CLI's order is exercised by tests. Solution: pin the missing case first (probe `ml record --type pattern --evidence-issue X` and compare) before touching CANONICAL_ORDER; then let one writer own the layout. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

title: Split doctor into reader, catalog, and repair
description: Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 5, Worth exploring). Evidence: doctor.rs is 653 lines doing read+decide+mutate+render; `--fix` re-reads the domain files, re-derives staleness with its own copy of the rule, and re-implements the 0-byte rewrite; 11 of the 17 checks are hardcoded pass literals. Solution: extract the shared domain-file reader (reuse the status/records policy) so the repair pass stops re-reading and re-parsing; separate the check catalog from the repair executor. Report: /tmp/architecture-review-1791062327.html.

title: record upsert semantics: named-type duplicates update in place (not an anonymous advisory)
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind; pre-existing since mulch-fdd0). Reference `commands/record.ts:1085-1130`: a duplicate on pattern/decision/reference/guide UPSERTS in place and prints `✓ Updated existing <type> in <domain> (record #N)`; the batch path reports `updated` in its counters. Ours always prints `Duplicate <type> already exists in <domain> (record #N). Use --force to add anyway.` and writes nothing; batch counts it as `skipped`. Also: the dedupe key is wrong — the reference `findDuplicate` (utils/expertise.ts:194-217) compares the TYPE'S DEDUP FIELD, ours compares the id, so a store holding a renamed record (which `edit --name` produces, since neither side recomputes ids) gets a second appended record where the reference upserts one. Evidence: 3-way probes in the sprint-4 spec review (/tmp/review, report lines 2-3).

title: edit/outcome: record-id resolution (bare hash, unique prefix, ambiguous) like delete/move
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind). `edit <domain> 1bb21d` / `outcome <domain> 1bb21d` fail with `Record "1bb21d" not found.` where the reference resolves bare hashes, unique prefixes and reports `Ambiguous identifier … Use more characters to disambiguate.`; the lib already ships `resolve_record_id` (records.rs) and delete/move use it. Evidence: `identifier_resolution_matches_reference` (cli_parity.rs) covers delete/move only.

title: outcome without --status must be read-only (list, never append)
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review — and it MUTATES the store. Reference `commands/outcome.ts:41-102`: with no `--status` it prints `No outcomes recorded for this record.` (or lists the existing ones) and writes nothing. Ours has no such branch: it appends `{"recorded_at": …}` (no status ⇒ a schema-invalid outcome), prints `✓ Outcome recorded: success on <id>` and the json envelope claims `"action":"appended"`. Battery-blind: `outcome_matches_reference` only exercises `--status`.

title: record stdin/batch: reference rewrites compactly and its counters/plain surface differ
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind, pre-existing). Reference `record.ts:420` calls `writeExpertiseFile` for the batch path (compact rewrite, comments/blanks dropped, ids generated for id-less survivors); ours appends per line, so any non-canonical store stays byte-different. Counter/summary surface: within-batch duplicates (reference dry-run created 2/skipped 0 vs ours 1/1), `Skip: N` vs `Create: 0` in the dry-run summary, `Would process` counts created+updated (ours created+skipped), the plain `Skipped N duplicate(s) in <domain>` line, no `✓ Created 0 record(s)` line when nothing was created, json dry-run missing `updated`/`errors`/`warnings`, and the validation-error text shape (`Validation errors:` then indented entries; bare AJV text per entry).

title: edit: validate the UPDATED record against the schema before writing
description: Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (low severity, higher consequence after the compact-rewrite change). The reference validates the updated record and refuses writes that would persist schema-invalid content (`Error: updated record failed schema validation …`), and refuses adding unknown extra fields; ours writes both. Also the legacy singular `outcome` field: the reference ABORTS such an edit, we normalize it to `outcomes` on rewrite (documented in README DEVIATIONS).
